pains.statement: Confirming tomorrow's appointments means sending dozens of WhatsApp messages by hand, which takes most of the morning.
pains.quote: One by one. I copy the name, the time, the dentist, paste it in a message and send it.

pains.statement: Many patients ignore confirmation messages, so the receptionist has to follow up with phone calls.
pains.quote: Half of them don't answer. So in the afternoon I call the ones who didn't reply.

pains.statement: Patients who confirmed still don't show up, leaving dentists idle.
pains.quote: And even when they say yes, some still don't come. Yesterday we had four no-shows.

pains.statement: Offering a cancelled slot to people waiting for an earlier appointment is manual and too slow, so the slot usually goes unused.
pains.quote: I have to call each one and by the time someone says yes, the time has passed. Most of the time the slot just stays empty.

pains.statement: Handling reschedule requests by phone is slow and keeps the line busy for other patients.
pains.quote: I have to check the dentist's agenda, the room, and it takes forever while the line is ringing again.

pains.statement: Keeping a paper agenda alongside the software leads to double bookings.
pains.quote: Last month I booked two patients at the same time with him because the paper one wasn't updated.

pains.statement: Every no-show or late cancellation is professional time the clinic pays for and cannot bill.
pains.quote: If a patient doesn't show up, that's 50 minutes I'm paying the professional for and getting nothing.

pains.statement: The system has no report on no-shows or empty slots, so the owner rebuilds it in Excel at month end, when it's too late to act.
pains.quote: there's no report of who didn't come, which professional has more empty slots, which day of the week is worse.

pains.statement: Without data on patterns, the owner can't take targeted actions such as asking repeat no-show patients for a deposit.
pains.quote: If I knew a specific patient misses all the time, I'd ask for a deposit. Today I'm flying blind.

pains.statement: Each unit only sees its own agenda, so patients are turned away while the other unit has free slots.
pains.quote: the receptionist doesn't know that unit B has three free slots that afternoon. We lose the patient to a competitor because of that.

pains.statement: Cancellation fees are hard to enforce manually and create conflict with patients, so they are never charged.
pains.quote: The receptionist has to remember, call the patient, it creates conflict. In the end nobody charged it.

pains.statement: SMS reminders are expensive and patients don't answer them because they use WhatsApp.
pains.quote: it's expensive per message and the patients don't reply to SMS anyway.

pains.statement: Physiotherapists learn about cancellations only when they are already waiting, so they can't use the time.
pains.quote: They complain that they find out about cancellations only when they're already waiting for the patient.

pains.statement: Booking requires calling during a short window, and the line is often busy.
pains.quote: I called three times during my lunch break and the line was always busy.

pains.statement: The clinic can only be reached during business hours, which overlap with the patient's own working hours.
pains.quote: At night, when I actually have time to organise the family's agenda, there's nobody there.

pains.statement: Reminders sent two days before are too early to prevent a busy parent from forgetting.
pains.quote: two days before doesn't help me — I need a reminder on the day, a few hours before.

pains.statement: Rescheduling requires another call, so the patient sometimes skips the appointment instead of cancelling.
pains.quote: Sometimes I just give up and don't go, which I know isn't fair to the clinic.

pains.statement: Patients aren't told when the doctor is running late and wait a long time at the clinic.
pains.quote: Nobody told us the doctor was running late.

pains.statement: The schedule only blocks the doctor's time, not rooms or shared equipment, so the receptionist tracks the machine in a separate spreadsheet.
pains.quote: The system only blocks the doctor's time. So I keep a separate spreadsheet for the machine.

pains.statement: Equipment conflicts make patients wait, leave and post bad public reviews.
pains.quote: One patient waited an hour and left. She posted a bad review on Google.

pains.statement: Preparation instructions for procedures are sent by hand and sometimes forgotten, so the patient arrives unprepared and the slot is lost.
pains.quote: Sometimes I forget, and the patient arrives unprepared and we have to reschedule. The whole slot is lost.

pains.statement: The waiting list for long procedure slots runs on a WhatsApp group, which is a privacy risk and chaotic.
pains.quote: I'm not supposed to use a group like that because of privacy. And whoever answers first gets it, it's chaos.

pains.statement: Online self-booking could break procedure rules such as room, equipment or a required prior evaluation.
pains.quote: For procedures I'm afraid, because they'd book without the room or the machine, or without the evaluation they need first.

pains.statement: Apps with complex passwords and email verification codes lock out older patients.
pains.quote: It asked for a password with capital letters and numbers, and then it sent a code to an email I don't check. I gave up.

pains.statement: Small text in apps is hard to read for older patients.
pains.quote: The letters are tiny too.

pains.statement: Phone calls to the clinic often take long to be answered.
pains.quote: sometimes it takes a long time for them to answer, and I have to call back.

pains.statement: Schedule changes are communicated only on arrival, so the patient makes a wasted trip.
pains.quote: I took two buses to get there for nothing.

pains.statement: The owner still needs a spreadsheet to know the number of no-shows.
pains.quote: I still need a spreadsheet to know how many no-shows I had.

pains.statement: Sending WhatsApp confirmations one by one takes the receptionist's whole morning.
pains.quote: Sending confirmations one by one on WhatsApp takes my whole morning.

pains.statement: Rooms are not part of the schedule, which allows double bookings of the same room.
pains.quote: Two patients were booked in the same room at 3pm because the room is not part of the schedule, only the professional.

pains.statement: Patients can't reschedule without calling the clinic.
pains.quote: Impossible to reschedule without calling. I tried for two days.

pains.statement: Owners can't see the agenda of their other unit.
pains.quote: I can't see the agenda of my other unit from this one.

pains.statement: A reminder one hour before the appointment is too late for the patient to reorganise.
pains.quote: Received the reminder at 7am for an appointment at 8am. Way too late to reorganise my day.

pains.statement: Professionals only learn about a cancellation when they are already waiting.
pains.quote: I only know a patient cancelled when I'm already waiting for them.

pains.statement: Password recovery fails, pushing patients back to the phone.
pains.quote: Created an account, forgot the password, the reset email never arrived.

pains.statement: There's no quick way to offer a cancelled slot to the waiting list.
pains.quote: When someone cancels I have no fast way to offer the slot to the waiting list.

themes.title: Confirmations and reminders don't work
themes.description: Confirming appointments is manual, costly and badly timed: front desks spend hours on it, many patients never answer, and reminders arrive too early or too late to change behaviour.

themes.title: No-shows waste paid professional time
themes.description: Patients miss appointments even after confirming, and clinics have no practical way to discourage it, so paid professional hours go unbilled.

themes.title: Cancelled slots are rarely refilled
themes.description: When a slot frees up, offering it to people who want an earlier time is manual, slow and sometimes privacy-unsafe, so the slot is usually lost.

themes.title: Booking and rescheduling depend on the phone
themes.description: Patients can only book or move appointments by calling during business hours; lines are busy, receptionists are overloaded and some patients simply skip instead of rescheduling.

themes.title: Agenda ignores rooms and equipment
themes.description: The schedule only tracks professionals, so rooms, shared machines and procedure rules live in side spreadsheets or paper, causing double bookings and angry patients.

themes.title: Units can't see each other's availability
themes.description: Multi-unit clinics run separate agendas, so a patient is turned away at one unit while another has free slots.

themes.title: Owners can't see where the agenda loses money
themes.description: There is no reporting on no-shows, idle slots or patterns, so owners rebuild numbers in Excel after the fact and can't act on them.

themes.title: Changes and delays reach people too late
themes.description: Cancellations, delays and time changes are not communicated proactively, so professionals sit idle and patients wait or travel for nothing.

themes.title: Digital access excludes less tech-savvy patients
themes.description: Passwords, email codes and small text make apps unusable for some patients, who fall back to the phone.

opportunities.title: Patients confirm or release their slot without front-desk effort
opportunities.how_might_we: How might we get every patient to confirm or free their slot in time, without the receptionist sending a single message by hand?
opportunities.rationale: Strongest signal in the research: mentioned in 5 of 6 sources by receptionists, owners and patients, with high severity (no-shows rated 5). Saves hours of receptionist time daily and directly protects revenue. WhatsApp is the channel every persona already uses.
opportunities.hypothesis: We believe that automatic WhatsApp confirmations sent at the right time for small clinics will reduce no-shows and manual work. We will know when the no-show rate drops by 30% and manual confirmation messages fall close to zero within 6 weeks.

opportunities.title: Patients can book and reschedule by themselves, at any time
opportunities.how_might_we: How might we let patients book and move appointments when it suits them, without calling, and without excluding less digital patients?
opportunities.rationale: Mentioned in 5 sources and closely linked to no-shows (patients skip instead of rescheduling). Effort is high because clinic rules (procedures, rooms) must be respected and the experience must work for seniors without passwords; effort estimate is uncertain.
opportunities.hypothesis: We believe that a password-free self-service link to book and reschedule for patients will reduce phone volume and silent no-shows. We will know when 40% of reschedules happen without a call.

opportunities.title: Freed slots are refilled before they go to waste
opportunities.how_might_we: How might we offer a freed slot to the right waiting patient within minutes, fairly and without exposing personal data?
opportunities.rationale: Raised by both receptionists and the feedback batch; especially painful for long procedure slots. Confidence is moderate (3 mentions) but effort is low if built on top of automated confirmations.
opportunities.hypothesis: We believe that automatically offering cancelled slots to a waiting list for receptionists will recover lost appointments. We will know when at least 30% of cancelled slots are refilled.

opportunities.title: The agenda knows every resource a booking needs
opportunities.how_might_we: How might we make the schedule aware of rooms, equipment, units and procedure rules so that conflicts become impossible?
opportunities.rationale: Double bookings are severe (lost patients, public bad reviews) and appear in 4 sources, but mostly in procedure-heavy and multi-unit clinics. Larger change to the scheduling core, so effort is high.
opportunities.hypothesis: We believe that resource-aware scheduling for clinics with procedures or several units will eliminate double bookings. We will know when resource conflicts reported to support drop to zero.

opportunities.title: Everyone affected learns about changes as soon as they happen
opportunities.how_might_we: How might we tell patients and professionals about cancellations, delays and time changes the moment they happen?
opportunities.rationale: Mentioned in 4 sources by patients and physiotherapists. Lower business impact per event, but cheap to deliver once notifications exist, and it prevents wasted trips that damage trust.
opportunities.hypothesis: We believe that real-time change notifications for patients and professionals will reduce wasted trips and idle time. We will know when complaints about late notice disappear from NPS comments.

opportunities.title: Owners see where the schedule loses money
opportunities.how_might_we: How might we show owners, without spreadsheets, how much the agenda loses and where?
opportunities.rationale: Comes from owners (the buyers) in an interview and an NPS 4 detractor; ties directly to retention. Fewer mentions so lower confidence; mostly reporting on data we already have.
opportunities.hypothesis: We believe that a no-show and occupancy dashboard for clinic owners will increase perceived value. We will know when owners' NPS rises and Excel exports drop.

stories.title: Automatic WhatsApp confirmation request
stories.want: the system to send each patient a WhatsApp confirmation request automatically before their appointment
stories.so_that: I stop spending my mornings sending messages by hand and can focus on patients at the desk

acceptance_criteria.given: an appointment scheduled for tomorrow at 10:00
acceptance_criteria.when: the configured send time arrives (default: 24 hours before)
acceptance_criteria.then: the patient receives a WhatsApp message with date, time, professional and Confirm / Reschedule / Cancel options

acceptance_criteria.given: the patient taps Confirm
acceptance_criteria.then: the appointment status changes to Confirmed in the agenda without any action from the receptionist

acceptance_criteria.given: the patient has not replied
acceptance_criteria.when: 4 hours have passed since the request
acceptance_criteria.then: a single follow-up message is sent and the appointment is highlighted as Unconfirmed in the agenda

acceptance_criteria.given: the patient has no valid WhatsApp number
acceptance_criteria.then: the appointment is flagged for a manual call and appears in the receptionist's to-do list

stories.notes: Validate the default send time per clinic type (procedures may need 48h for preparation). Requires WhatsApp Business API costs to be checked against the SMS cost Marcos complained about.

stories.title: Day-of reminder at a patient-friendly time
stories.want: a reminder on the day of my appointment, a few hours before it
stories.so_that: I don't forget and still have time to reorganise my day if needed

acceptance_criteria.given: a confirmed appointment at 15:00
acceptance_criteria.when: it is 3 hours before the appointment
acceptance_criteria.then: I receive a WhatsApp reminder with the address and a Reschedule option

acceptance_criteria.given: an appointment before 10:00
acceptance_criteria.then: the reminder is sent at 19:00 the previous evening instead

acceptance_criteria.given: I already cancelled the appointment
acceptance_criteria.then: no reminder is sent

stories.notes: Assumes the reminder window can be configured per clinic. Check whether the add-to-calendar link Juliana asked for fits in this story or a separate one.

stories.title: Join the waiting list for an earlier slot
stories.want: to add a patient to a waiting list for a professional or procedure with their preferred days and times
stories.so_that: I have an organised, private list to offer freed slots instead of a notebook or a WhatsApp group

acceptance_criteria.given: a patient asks for an earlier appointment
acceptance_criteria.when: I add them to the waiting list with professional, procedure and preferred periods
acceptance_criteria.then: they appear in the list ordered by request date

acceptance_criteria.given: a patient on the waiting list books a regular appointment
acceptance_criteria.then: they are removed from the waiting list automatically

acceptance_criteria.given: a receptionist without permission for patient data
acceptance_criteria.then: only names and preferences are shown, never phone numbers of other patients

stories.notes: Validate with Carla whether procedure prerequisites (prior evaluation) must be checked when adding to the list. LGPD: no shared groups.

stories.title: Offer a cancelled slot to the waiting list automatically
stories.want: a cancelled slot to be offered automatically to matching patients on the waiting list
stories.so_that: the slot gets refilled in minutes instead of staying empty

acceptance_criteria.given: a slot is cancelled at least 2 hours in advance
acceptance_criteria.when: there are matching patients on the waiting list
acceptance_criteria.then: the first 3 in order receive a WhatsApp offer with an Accept link

acceptance_criteria.given: two patients accept the same offer
acceptance_criteria.then: the second patient is told the slot was taken and stays on the waiting list

acceptance_criteria.given: nobody accepts within 30 minutes
acceptance_criteria.then: the next 3 patients on the list receive the offer

acceptance_criteria.given: the slot requires a room or machine
acceptance_criteria.then: it is only offered if the resource is still free

stories.notes: Depends on story US01 (WhatsApp messaging). Offer size and expiry time are assumptions to test.

stories.title: Notify the professional when a patient cancels
stories.want: to be notified as soon as one of my patients cancels
stories.so_that: I can use the time for paperwork or another patient instead of waiting

acceptance_criteria.given: a patient cancels today's appointment
acceptance_criteria.when: the cancellation is registered by the patient or the receptionist
acceptance_criteria.then: I receive a notification within 1 minute with the freed time

acceptance_criteria.given: the cancellation is for a future day
acceptance_criteria.then: it appears in my agenda but no instant notification is sent

acceptance_criteria.given: I have turned notifications off
acceptance_criteria.then: only the agenda is updated

stories.notes: Channel for professionals (app push vs WhatsApp) to be validated.

stories.title: Tell patients about delays and time changes before they leave home
stories.want: to receive a message when my appointment is delayed or changed
stories.so_that: I don't wait for nothing or make a wasted trip

acceptance_criteria.given: the receptionist marks a professional as running 30 minutes late
acceptance_criteria.then: all patients for the next 2 hours receive a WhatsApp message with the new estimated time

acceptance_criteria.given: the clinic changes my appointment time
acceptance_criteria.then: I receive a message with the new time and a Confirm / Reschedule option

acceptance_criteria.given: I don't confirm a time change
acceptance_criteria.then: the receptionist sees an alert to call me

stories.notes: Messages must use large, simple text and no login, so that senior patients like Pedro can act on them.
